Create a blank Account-owned Canvas document. Use documents.execute to add or inspect design content.
operations.instructions: Creation accepts a title only and produces the same minimal blank document as the Canvas UI: one white 720×480 starter frame. The result identifies that frame as `starterFrameId`; replace or update it when building the first screen so it does not remain underneath new content. Creation does not open a tab or import `.pen` JSON. Call documents.execute for content, then documents.open when visible review matters.

operations.summary: Read or change one Canvas document with bounded Pencil-style JavaScript; one execution should express one coherent design intent.
operations.instructions:
Execute runs JavaScript against a private document clone. Available globals are Get, Insert, Copy, Update, Replace, Delete, Move, G, TakeScreenshot, and Print; the script cannot access files, network, Account data, timers, or the Penkra runtime directly. Selectors are exact: `#node-id`, `type:frame`, `name:Header`, `*`, a slash-separated ID path, or an unprefixed exact node ID. Get returns immutable contexts with node, parent, index, path, resolved pre-execution bounds, and problems; its optional limit defaults to 1,000 and cannot exceed 1,000.

Insert(parent, node, position) adds one node tree; use null for the document root. A newly created document already has the exact `starterFrameId` returned by documents.create; replace or update that frame for the first screen instead of inserting overlapping content. Update changes properties without replacing ID or children. Copy renews IDs recursively. Replace, Delete, and Move each require exactly one target. Print records bounded JSON values in the result.

G(target, "ai", prompt) generates a low-quality GPT Image 2 asset using Canvas's global image-generation service. G(target, source) applies an absolute path, file:// URL, HTTP(S) URL, or data URL. Canvas stores the image before commit and replaces the transient source with a durable document asset; a new relative path is rejected unless it already names an uploaded asset.

TakeScreenshot([target, ...]) renders one or more exact nodes together as a PNG and returns it as image content with dimensions in `screenshots`. Call it after the mutations it should verify, as in `const screen = Replace("#starter-frame-id", {...}); TakeScreenshot([screen]);`. It renders document content through Canvas's Pencil-compatible engine; it does not capture editor chrome and does not require an open or visible tab.

For library icons, insert a native `type: "icon"` node with exact `library` and `icon` fields. Valid libraries are `lucide`, `feather`, `Material Symbols Outlined`, `Material Symbols Rounded`, `Material Symbols Sharp`, and `phosphor`. Set width, height, and fill explicitly.

A script may be at most 100,000 UTF-8 bytes and runs for at most five seconds with a 64 MiB heap and 4 MiB stack. Canvas validates the complete result and commits only when the source sequence is unchanged. A read-only execution returns `operationId: null`; a successful mutation returns the durable `operationId` accepted by documents.undo while that operation remains the document head. Any later edit invalidates it. Use one execution for one coherent design intent. Inspect relevant structure with Get and use TakeScreenshot whenever appearance matters. Never blindly replay a CANVAS_DOCUMENT_CHANGED failure.

examples.name: Inspect frames with resolved bounds and problems

input.code: return Get("type:frame", ({ node, parent, bounds, problems }) => Print({ id: node.id, name: node.name ?? null, parentId: parent?.id ?? null, bounds, problems }), { limit: 100 });

Insert(null, { id: "sign-in", type: "frame", name: "Sign in", x: 0, y: 0, width: 393, height: 852, layout: "vertical", padding: 24, gap: 16, fill: "#ffffff", children: [] });
return "sign-in";

operations.summary: Undo the latest agent documents.execute mutation while it remains the exact document head.
operations.instructions: This reverses one complete mutating documents.execute operation; it does not manipulate the editor's local undo stack and does not reconstruct an older document. Pass the returned operationId when available. If an execute call timed out after committing and its result was lost, omit operationId to resolve and undo the exact current head agent operation. Canvas rejects the request if a UI, collaborator, or later agent edit has advanced the document, if the operation was already undone, or if the caller did not author it. After rejection, inspect the current document instead of guessing or replaying stale changes.

documentId.description: Exact document containing the agent operation to undo.

operationId.description: Durable operationId returned by the mutating documents.execute call. Omit only when its result was lost after a possible commit.

operations.summary: Open one exact Canvas document in a new or explicitly targeted tab for the user.
operations.instructions: Opening changes visible tab state but does not modify document content. Use documents.execute with TakeScreenshot for document visual inspection; open a tab when the user should view or work in the Canvas editor.

examples.name: Open a document for visual review

operations.summary: Move one owned Canvas document to recoverable Trash after explicit user authorization and exact current-title confirmation.
operations.instructions: Resolve the exact current title with documents.list, obtain explicit authorization to move that document to Trash, and pass the title unchanged as confirmTitle. Edit or cleanup authorization does not imply moving the document to Trash. Agents cannot permanently delete Canvas documents.

examples.name: Move an explicitly confirmed test document to Trash
